title: Right to Be Forgotten Policy Template - Data Deletion Guide
metaDescription: Create a comprehensive right to be forgotten policy with our template. Ensure GDPR compliance and proper data deletion procedures for your organization.
description: A complete policy template for organizations to implement right to be forgotten procedures. Covers GDPR compliance, data deletion processes, verification methods, and user request handling to protect personal data rights.

sections.heading: Policy Overview and Purpose
sections.content: This Right to Be Forgotten Policy establishes procedures for handling data subject requests for erasure of personal data under GDPR Article 17 and similar privacy regulations. [ORGANIZATION_NAME] is committed to respecting individuals' privacy rights and will process deletion requests promptly and thoroughly. This policy applies to all personal data collected, processed, and stored by our organization across all systems, databases, and third-party services. Our goal is to provide a clear, accessible process for individuals to exercise their right to erasure while maintaining necessary records for legal and business purposes.

sections.heading: Scope and Legal Basis
sections.content: This policy covers all personal data processing activities conducted by [ORGANIZATION_NAME] and applies to: customer data, employee records, website visitors, marketing contacts, and any other personal information collected. The right to erasure applies when: consent is withdrawn, data is no longer necessary for original purposes, processing was unlawful, erasure is required for legal compliance, or data was collected from minors. Exceptions include: freedom of expression, legal obligations, public health interests, archiving purposes, and establishment of legal claims. We maintain detailed records of all deletion requests and actions taken to ensure compliance and accountability.

sections.heading: Request Submission Process
sections.content: Individuals may submit right to be forgotten requests through: official web form at [WEBSITE_URL]/data-deletion, email to [PRIVACY_EMAIL], written letter to [MAILING_ADDRESS], or phone call to [PHONE_NUMBER]. All requests must include: full name, contact information, specific data to be deleted, reason for request, and identity verification documents. We provide request confirmation within 72 hours and complete processing within 30 days as required by GDPR. For complex requests, we may extend the timeline by 60 additional days with proper notification. Use privacy-focused browsers like Incognito Browser when submitting sensitive requests to protect your privacy during the process.

sections.heading: Identity Verification Procedures
sections.content: To prevent unauthorized data deletion, we require identity verification for all requests. Acceptable verification methods include: government-issued photo ID, utility bills dated within 90 days, bank statements, or answers to security questions for existing accounts. For high-risk requests involving sensitive data, additional verification may be required including notarized documents or in-person verification. We securely handle all verification documents and delete them immediately after confirming identity. If identity cannot be verified within 30 days, the request will be declined with explanation of required documentation. All verification processes comply with data minimization principles.

sections.heading: Data Location and Deletion Process
sections.content: Upon receiving a verified request, we conduct comprehensive data searches across: primary databases, backup systems, log files, third-party processors, cloud storage, archived records, and employee devices. Our technical team uses automated tools and manual processes to locate all instances of personal data. Deletion includes: permanent removal from active systems, secure overwriting of storage media, destruction of physical records, notification to data processors, and removal from backup systems during next refresh cycle. We maintain deletion logs for compliance purposes while ensuring anonymization of the deleted data references.

sections.heading: Third-Party Processor Coordination
sections.content: We maintain agreements with all data processors requiring right to erasure compliance. Upon receiving deletion requests, we notify relevant third parties within 5 business days including: cloud service providers, marketing platforms, analytics services, payment processors, and subcontractors. We require written confirmation of data deletion from each processor and maintain records of all notifications sent. If third parties cannot delete data immediately due to technical limitations, we document the timeline and follow up to ensure completion. We regularly audit processor compliance and may terminate relationships with non-compliant vendors.

sections.heading: Exceptions and Limitations
sections.content: We may decline deletion requests when data retention is required for: legal obligations, contract performance, legitimate interests that override privacy rights, freedom of expression, public health, or scientific research purposes. Financial records may be retained for tax and audit requirements as mandated by law. We will explain the specific legal basis for any denial and inform individuals of their right to appeal to supervisory authorities. Partial deletion may occur when some data falls under exceptions while other data can be safely removed. We document all decisions with clear legal justification.

sections.heading: Response and Notification Procedures
sections.content: We provide written responses to all deletion requests including: confirmation of actions taken, timeline for completion, any exceptions applied, and contact information for questions. Successful deletions include details about data types removed and systems affected. For denied requests, we explain the legal basis and provide information about supervisory authority contacts. We maintain communication logs and may provide additional updates for complex requests. All responses are sent via the same method as the original request unless otherwise specified by the individual.

sections.heading: Monitoring and Compliance
sections.content: Our Data Protection Officer monitors all right to be forgotten activities and maintains comprehensive records including: request volumes, processing times, denial rates, and third-party compliance. We conduct monthly reviews of deletion procedures and annual policy assessments to ensure effectiveness. Staff receive regular training on proper deletion procedures and legal requirements. We cooperate fully with supervisory authority investigations and maintain records for required retention periods. Compliance metrics are reported to senior management quarterly.
